As a result showingLast is false, the next control is enabled, and clicking it sets offset to user_count, loading an empty second page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), preserving the existing zero-member special case."

      "body": "GroupsController#members is reachable without authentication for any visible group. limit is taken directly from params[:limit] with no upper bound and no positive-integer validation. A request such as /groups/some-group/members.json?limit=100000000 forces the server to construct and serialize a huge result set, causing database load and memory exhaustion. Cap limit to a small maximum and reject values <= 0."
    },

      "body": "Previously /groups/:group_id/members returned a JSON array of serialized users. It now returns an object with members and meta. Existing consumers of this public route that expect a top-level array will break. The SPA client was updated, but this is an unversioned contract change to a public API path."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb",
      "line": 38,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "PATCH update semantics were removed but PATCH still routes to update",
      "body": "The old update distinguished request.patch? and processed params[:changes] for incremental membership changes. The new update ignores changes, so a PATCH request (which resources :groups still routes to this action) will not add or remove members. Worse, because params[:visible] is absent, group.visible is set to false. Existing PATCH clients can silently hide a group and receive a success response."
    },

      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs",
      "line": 1,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Automatic group check evaluates against member user instead of group",
      "body": "group_member.hbs is used as the itemView for each member in {{each member in members itemView=\"group-member\"}}, so the template context is the member User object, not the group. User has no automatic property, so automatic is undefined/falsy and {{#unless automatic}} renders the remove link even for automatic groups. The server rejects removal with 422, but the UI exposes a control that fails with no client-side error handling."

findings.title: totalPages off by one for exact multiples of limit
findings.body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (for example 50 with the default limit 50), this returns 2 instead of 1. As a result showingLast is false, the next control is enabled, and clicking it sets offset to user_count, loading an empty second page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), preserving the existing zero-member special case.

findings.title: Unbounded public group member query limit
findings.body: GroupsController#members is reachable without authentication for any visible group. limit is taken directly from params[:limit] with no upper bound and no positive-integer validation. A request such as /groups/some-group/members.json?limit=100000000 forces the server to construct and serialize a huge result set, causing database load and memory exhaustion. Cap limit to a small maximum and reject values <= 0.

findings.title: Public members endpoint response shape changed from array to object
findings.body: Previously /groups/:group_id/members returned a JSON array of serialized users. It now returns an object with members and meta. Existing consumers of this public route that expect a top-level array will break. The SPA client was updated, but this is an unversioned contract change to a public API path.

findings.title: PATCH update semantics were removed but PATCH still routes to update
findings.body: The old update distinguished request.patch? and processed params[:changes] for incremental membership changes. The new update ignores changes, so a PATCH request (which resources :groups still routes to this action) will not add or remove members. Worse, because params[:visible] is absent, group.visible is set to false. Existing PATCH clients can silently hide a group and receive a success response.

findings.title: Automatic group check evaluates against member user instead of group
findings.body: group_member.hbs is used as the itemView for each member in {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}, so the template context is the member User object, not the group. User has no automatic property, so automatic is undefined/falsy and {{#unless automatic}} renders the remove link even for automatic groups. The server rejects removal with 422, but the UI exposes a control that fails with no client-side error handling.

findings.title: Automatic remove_member test uses PUT instead of DELETE
findings.body: The route for remove_member is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member" and the client sends DELETE. This spec calls xhr :put, :remove_member. Because controller specs dispatch the given action directly, the test does not verify that the production HTTP verb is routable and could pass even if the DELETE route is broken or removed. It should use xhr :delete, :remove_member.
